One piece of ID with your name and Toronto address is enough. A driver’s licence, utility bill, credit card statement or tax form all work. Photo ID isn’t required. items.title: Strap in for what’s expected to be a tight mayoral race in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga isn’t used to close mayoral races, but by all accounts it has one now. m. tonight, voters will soon determine if the contest among the current mayor, her predecessor and two city councillors is a tight affair, as expected, or if one of the hopefuls unexpectedly claims a decisive victory. The 2026 mayoral campaign in Mississauga started with two clear-cut favourites in incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie, the latter leaving the post early in 2024 after a decade-long run to take the reins of Ontario’s Liberal Party. City councillors Alvin Tedjo (Ward 2) and Dipika Damerla (Ward 7) also brought recognizable names — and resumes — to the campaign, but neither was initially expected to mount a serious challenge to the two favourites. However, several recent polls suggest Tedjo has made strong enough gains to turn the race into a three-candidate contest heading down the home stretch. Whatever the end result, the 2026 run for mayor in Canada’s seventh-largest city has provided residents and political watchers alike with some interesting dynamics. Randy Besco, an associate professor of political science at University of Toronto Mississauga, told INSAUGA Canada in an interview it’s unusual in municipal politics for an incumbent mayor to face a challenge from her predecessor. In effect, he noted, it’s like having “two incumbents” compete for the mayor’s seat.

items.title: Cold temperatures prompt weather alert for Toronto, Mississauga, and Brampton
items.summary: Chilly conditions are in the forecast, which has prompted a weather alert for parts of the Greater Toronto Area. Environment Canada has issued a yellow frost advisory for Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Burlington, and Oakville. For Toronto, Mississauga, and Brampton, forecasters said patchy frost is expected to develop overnight into Tuesday morning, particularly for areas north of the 401 corridor. In Burlington and Oakville, the alert said frost is expected to develop overnight, particularly for areas along and north of the 407 corridor. “Damage to plants, trees, and crops is possible,” Environment Canada said. “Take preventative measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees, and crops. ” The coldest conditions are expected in Mississauga and Brampton, where a low of just 1 C is expected. Toronto, Burlington, and Oakville have a low of 2 C in the forecast.

items.title: 5 things to know about 30-storey rental tower in Mississauga
items.summary: The building will feature 315 rental units. A 315-home purpose-built rental development recently broke ground in Port Credit. Edenshaw Developments broke ground Oct. 8 on a 30-storey purpose-built rental development in Mississauga’s Port Credit neighbourhood. Here are five key details about the project: The site is located at 23 Elizabeth St. N. and 42-46 Park St. E. The project is expected to support hundreds of construction jobs. Construction is expected to take about three years, with completion anticipated in 2029. The 30-storey building will feature 315 rental units, including 51 barrier-free suites. The project will offer a mix of one-bedroom, one-bedroom-plus-den and two-bedroom suites. Amenities will include a gym, cold plunge, infrared sauna, indoor/outdoor entertaining spaces, a pet spa and an outdoor dog run.

items.title: Nearly 560,000 Mississauga Residents Eligible to Vote as Polls Open Monday
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports Mississauga residents head to the polls Monday, Oct. 26, to elect the city's mayor, their ward and regional councillor, and school board trustees for the 2026-2030 term. According to the city, there were 559,661 voters on the Mississauga voters' list as of Oct. 14, and 44,049 of them had already cast ballots during the advance polling period. The outlet reports voters can view the full list of candidates on the city's election website before heading to their polling station. According to the outlet, unofficial results will be posted to that same website once polls close Monday evening. The outlet reports residents can confirm where and how to vote, including what identification to bring, through the city's election resources before casting their ballot.

items.title: Voters across Ontario head to the polls for municipal elections
items.summary: The election is headlined by mayoral races in Toronto, Mississauga and Ottawa, with recent polls showing all three to be closely fought. Voters line up outside a voting station to cast their ballot in the Toronto’s municipal election in Toronto on Monday, October 22, 2018. It’s election day in Ontario, with voters in more than 400 municipalities set to pick their local representatives. The election is headlined by mayoral races in Toronto, Mississauga and Ottawa, with recent polls showing all three to be closely fought. Incumbent Olivia Chow is looking to hold off city councillor Brad Bradford in Toronto, while former Ontario Liberal leader Bonnie Crombie appears to be the front-runner to reclaim Mississauga’s top job in a race featuring councillor Alvin Tedjo and incumbent Carolyn Parrish. In Ottawa, city councillor Jeff Leiper is looking to unseat front-runner Mark Sutcliffe in a race that polls suggest has narrowed in the lead up to Monday’s election. Premier Doug Ford may not be on the ballot but his government’s changes figure prominently in local elections where candidates have sparred over strong mayor powers granted by the province. Olivia Chow and Brad Bradford are in a race for Toronto, while incumbent Carolyn Parrish, Bonnie Crombie, and Alvin Tedjo battle for Mississauga.

items.title: Clarkson Property Owner Hunts for Culprit After Second Illegal Dumping in Three Weeks
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the owner of the former Satellite restaurant property in Clarkson is trying to track down whoever keeps dumping construction waste on his land. According to the outlet, George Hantzakos says his site on Lakeshore Road West near Southdown Road has been targeted twice in under three weeks, with the most recent dumping on Oct. 24 leaving behind cinder blocks, bricks, broken concrete, metal rebar and what appeared to be pieces of a broken toilet. The outlet reports security footage from a neighbouring restaurant captured a dump truck pulling into the lot, backing up to unload the debris and then driving off westbound with its dump bed still partly raised. According to the outlet, police have been notified, and Hantzakos has been asking nearby businesses for additional camera footage that might help identify the truck. The outlet reports the incident follows an earlier dumping discovered on Oct. 8, which already cost Hantzakos $1,000 to have hauled away, leaving him now facing a second cleanup bill and damage to his parking area.

items.title: Man Dies After Early-Morning Stabbing, Peel Police Say Attacker Fled Scene
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a man has died after being stabbed in Mississauga in the early hours of Sunday, Oct. 25. According to Peel Regional Police, officers responded to a call reporting the stabbing and found a man who had been stabbed, and he was later pronounced dead from his injuries. The outlet reports the person responsible fled the area before officers arrived, and police currently have no description of a suspect to release. Police say the attack appears to have been an isolated incident rather than part of any broader threat to the public. According to the outlet, a large police presence remained in the area as investigators worked the scene, and nearby residents should expect road closures while the investigation continues. The victim's name has not been released. Police are asking anyone with information to call Peel Regional Police at 905-453-3311 and reference incident number PR260362288.
